title: Assessing a RISC-V Accelerator for Cross-Section Lookup in Chipyard
problem: Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations bottlenecked on cross-section lookups; Doppler broadening computations via Faddeeva function expensive in software
motivation: Design custom RISC-V accelerator to address cross-section lookup bottleneck; validate RISC-V for HPC through custom extension evaluation
method: They designed a specialized hardware accelerator based on RISC-V architecture, integrated with Chipyard's RocketCore processor design. The accelerator uses a pipelined design—where calculation stages overlap like an assembly line—combined with a Humlidek 8th-order rational approximation (a mathematical formula using polynomial ratios) to quickly compute the Faddeeva function for Doppler broadening (the temperature-dependent effects on particle collisions). They tested performance against software implementations on RISC-V and an Intel Core i5 Tiger Lake-U processor.
key_novelty: A specialized RISC-V hardware accelerator can speed up the cross-section calculations that bottleneck neutron transport simulations, demonstrating RISC-V's potential for high-performance computing.
contributions: Custom RISC-V accelerator design for cross-section lookups
Similar gains over Intel Core i5 Tiger Lake-U
Chipyard integration demonstrating HPC accelerator design
limitations: Limited to single kernel (Faddeeva); operating frequency optimization not yet done; scalability to additional kernels unclear; no power/energy analysis
